extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners learning algebraic and geometric solution methods (historical Italian treatise readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedures for reducing, transforming, and solving algebraic equations using arithmetic and geometric (area/square/rectangle) constructions; includes techniques to clear denominators, form squares, extract roots, and use oppositions/denominations. The material is from an historical Italian mathematical treatise and addresses step-by-step manipulations and geometric demonstrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce problems to earlier propositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Per che nota dx tutte le qftiói ppo Ae fono reducibiìi adalcu De li ppofti.6.capituli (note that all the questions can be reduced to some propositions of the preceding chapters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text emphasizes that many problems should be converted (reduced) to forms already treated in previous chapters. If an equation does not directly match the earlier proposition forms, transform it (by multiplying, adding, opposing, etc.) so it becomes one of those reducible cases; then apply the known solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use geometric demonstration for algebraic equations
rubrics_metrics.description: Demon Arario geometrica: give a geometric demonstration of the algebraic propositions (use areas, squares, rectangles to show equalities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whenever possible, translate algebraic equalities into geometrical constructions (areas of squares, rectangles, combinations of figures) and demonstrate truths by comparing those areas; e.g., reduce cubes or higher orders to areas that can be compared as squares or rectangles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express all quantities in the same unit
rubrics_metrics.description: Tu recata la eqtiatióe tutta a ... tu dimostri la quantità de le cofe quali ... (bring the equation entirely to the same unit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before performing algebraic manipulations, convert all terms so they share a common unit or denomination. This may require multiplying terms by factors so that all quantities are comparable and operations like addition/subtraction and forming squares are legitimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiply to clear denominators / obtain integral coefficients
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiplicbi in fe fa ... quando tu poni il numero che in la equatione fe troua:doe/j9.fara.é4*£ ... (multiply to remove fractional coefficients and make the coefficients whole).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If coefficients are fractional or denominated, multiply both sides by an appropriate number to clear denominators and obtain integers (or simpler coefficients) so that subsequent operations (forming squares, extraction of roots) are simpler. The treatise repeatedly advises multiplying to produce convenient units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add or subtract the same quantity to both sides
rubrics_metrics.description: Le parti si possono aumentare o diminuire ugualmente — addere o levare parti eguali da ambedue le parti dell'equazione.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use addition or subtraction of the same quantity on both sides to rearrange the equation (to collect like terms, to prepare for completing the square, or to place all terms on one side). The text gives many examples of moving quantities by adding/subtracting equally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form a square (complete the square) to solve quadratic-type relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Fare il quadrato: trasformare termini e somme in un qdrato (make the square) in modo da poter poi estrarre la radice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct squares (geometrically or algebraically) from given terms by arranging segments/areas (dividing sides, forming rectangles) so that the whole can be written as a perfect square; once in square form, take the square root to find the unknown. The treatise describes forming squares from combinations of rectangles and supplements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extract roots (radici) after forming a square
rubrics_metrics.description: Radice / radicarsi: dopo che la quantità è ridotta a quadrato, si estrae la radice per ottenere la quantità ignota.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once an expression has been successfully transformed into a perfect square, take the square root to recover the unknown. The text describes when and how the radical (root) is to be taken and warns about multiple possible outcomes or impossibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide lines/figures into parts to construct rectangles and squares
rubrics_metrics.description: Dividere la linea o la superficie in parti per fare rettangoli o quadrati utili alla dimostrazione e alla formazione del quadrato totale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric construction technique: subdivide sides into parts so that rectangles formed correspond to terms of the algebraic equation; by arranging these parts and their products one can build the square or other figure representing the equation. Many examples show dividing sides, applying complements/supplements, and recombining.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use opposition (opponere) to move and restore terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Oppofitione / restaurario: oppose parts of the equation (move terms to the other side) to restore the common unit or to make the whole comparable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The method of opposition consists in transferring a term from one side to the other (change of sign) to place the equation into a desired canonical form. The treatise explains oppositions as legitimate operations to equate extremes and means, and to bring the equation to a unitary magnitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denominate fractions to a common denominator before operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Denominatione: reduce fractions/rotti a comune denominatore prima di operare (denominate fractions to a common denominator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the equation contains fractional parts (rotti: binomio, trinomio, etc.), convert them to a common denominator (denominatione) and manipulate numerators accordingly. This is needed before multiplying, dividing, or forming squares; the text gives rules for multiplying numerator and denominator to attain the common measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat binomials/trinomials and their 'rotti' with component-wise multiplication
rubrics_metrics.description: I rotti binomio trinomio: operate on binomials/trinomials (and fractional forms) by multiplying their components appropriately to reduce them to known forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When algebraic expressions are binomial or trinomial (or fractional analogues), operate on their parts (components) according to the usual distributive/multiplicative rules so as to reduce the expression to a square or to rearrange terms; the treatise remarks that these composite forms require attention but follow the same principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare and equate surfaces (areas) to deduce algebraic equalities
rubrics_metrics.description: La superficie di un quadrato e l'altra superficie: se le superfici sono uguali, i quadrati o parti costruite su di esse sono corrispondentemente uguali.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate algebraic relations into equalities of plane figures: e.g., if two surfaces (constructed squares/rectangles) are equal, then the corresponding algebraic expressions equated to those areas are equal. The text repeatedly uses area-equality arguments to justify algebraic steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle cases with multiple remainders, impossible or extraneous solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Quando il numero non si può ridurre o si ottengono remanenti o radici impossibili: verificare e scartare i casi impossibili.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author warns about cases where reduction fails, where the extraction leads to impossible or extraneous roots, or where repeated remainders complicate progress. In such cases one must recognize impossibility or apply further transformations (multiplying, adding) or conclude that no simple rule applies; sometimes no fixed rule covers all such exceptional cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restore equality by supplementing or removing complementary figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Uso dei supplementi: applicare, togliere o confrontare supplementi di superficie per ottenere la figura desiderata (la quale cerca le altre cofe).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To form the square or other target figure one may need to add or remove supplements (supplementi) — small rectangles or squares attached to sides — so that the whole becomes a perfect square or decomposes into known areas. The technique is used in geometric completions and corresponding algebraic 'completing the square' maneuvers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceed by orderly prescribed rules (follow the sequence of operations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Le regole possono finire gl'ioni forsuere: bisogna procedere secondo l'ordine voluto, e osservare le parti delle operazioni e loro reciproche, proportio nalità e simili (follow the ordered rules and sequence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The treatise insists on following the prescribed order: convert units, denominate, multiply to clear fractions, apply oppositions, construct squares, extract roots. Deviating from the order may obscure the solution; the text lists elementary operations (addition, multiplication, extraction of roots, use of proportions) that should be in one's toolkit and applied in order.
